metric.capability_efficiency.basis: all-fragments (this worker measured every one of the 44 frozen probes for Java only; a common-basis figure requires the other 9 languages' fragment existence, which is out of scope for this shard and must be reconciled by the runner per interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule)

categories.context_dependent_rules: Count of rules whose application depends on information outside the immediate token (overload resolution, generic type inference at a call site, compiler flow-analysis such as definite-assignment or exhaustiveness checking, sealed-hierarchy membership checks).
categories.documented_semantic_exceptions: Count of JLS/JDK-documented departures from a 'normal' rule that a reader must already know to interpret the fragment correctly (e.g. 'array elements are default-initialized, unlike locals', 'unchecked exceptions need not be declared, unlike checked exceptions', 'subList returns a live view, unlike most collection factory methods', 'sealed permits enumerates the closed set exhaustively').
categories.implicit_rules: Count of behaviors that occur without an explicit token at the use site (autoboxing/unboxing, implicit numeric widening, silent integer overflow wraparound, default zero-initialization of array elements, unchecked-exception propagation without a declared clause, unspecified iteration order, view-vs-copy aliasing not signaled by the API name).
categories.syntax_forms: Count of distinct Java surface syntax constructs (declaration forms, operators, statements, expressions, annotations, generic-type syntax) that must appear in the measured_fragment (per capability_universe.json R5) to satisfy the canonical_task. Each distinct construct is counted once per probe even if repeated verbatim (e.g. two record declarations of the same kind in one probe count as 1 syntax form for 'record declaration', not 2), but two DIFFERENT constructs (e.g. a record declaration and a switch pattern-match) each count separately.

counting_methodology_frozen_before_annot.purpose: Per spec 6.1.4.E and the semantic-regularity evidence requirement (doc 20), the counting rule for each complexity category is fixed here before any per-probe annotation, so the per-probe unit counts below are audit-reproducible against this rule rather than against elegance judgement.
counting_methodology_frozen_before_annot.unit_value: Each occurrence recorded in any of the four categories above for a given probe contributes exactly 1 unit to that probe's complexity_units total. No sub-count is scored as 0 when it is genuinely absent for a probe (e.g. F03.P2 has 0 context_dependent_rules because list element assignment truly requires no non-local reasoning); a 0 here asserts 'this rule is not exercised by this fragment', which is a positive finding, not a missing-evidence placeholder. No 'unknown' was required anywhere in this shard because every category has directly reproducible JLS/JDK documentation for Java for all 44 probes.

metric.capability_efficiency.formula_used_here: normalized = 100 * (1 - min(E / E_max, 1)), E_max = 5.0 (frozen ceiling, documented above, applied identically in spirit to any language's shard)

gates.score_requires_comparability_gate: This is a single-language shard; the semantic-site comparability gate and the full 10-language Semantic Compression Overall Score/Ranking cannot be certified from this worker alone and must be certified by the runner after merging all language shards, per primary.json semantic_compression.score_requires_comparability_gate and worker_core.md rule 6.
gates.unfinished_applicable_work_is_not_na: All 44 probes were evaluated for Java; none were left as N/A. The 4 NONE probes carry written justifications per NA-6/support_rubric.levels.NONE, not N/A markers.

metric.capability_efficiency.note_on_normalization: This worker is language-sharded (Java only) per runner.max_requirement_ids_per_multi_language_agent constraints. True cross-language min-max normalization for Capability Efficiency requires all 10 languages' raw units-per-supported-capability-point figures, which are not available in this shard. The value reported below is a PROVISIONAL normalization computed from a frozen reference ceiling (E_max = 5.0 complexity units per supported capability point, chosen before any language's counting as a generous upper bound: max plausible per-probe unit count ~10 units over the 2 capability points a probe carries). The runner must recompute the final normalized score for Capability Efficiency once all language shards are merged, using the true cross-language distribution of raw E values; the raw E value for Java (1.7632) is preserved unmodified for that purpose.
